blocks.text: The oxides of nitrogen are NO, N2O, NO2, N2O4 and N2O5, in which the oxidation states of nitrogen range from +1 to +5. N2O4 and N2O5 decay quickly to other oxides. NO and NO2 are collectively called NOx. Their structures, properties and uses are given in Table 12.2.

blocks.caption: Properties of some common oxides of nitrogen (Table 12.2)
rows: colourless, water-soluble, neutral, sweet-smelling; helps combustion
dental anaesthetic; propellant for whipped cream; synthesis of NaN3
colourless, slightly soluble, neutral; NO paramagnetic, N2O2 diamagnetic; oxidising and reducing
biochemical messenger (lowers blood pressure); nitrosyl carbonyls
Nitrogen dioxide / dinitrogen tetroxide, NO2 / N2O4
NO2 reddish-brown, paramagnetic, reacts with water to give HNO3 and HNO2; N2O4 colourless liquid or solid; 2NO2 = N2O4 (cool to the right, heat to the left)
rocket propellant; HNO3 by the Ostwald process; explosives

blocks.alt: Electron-dot structures from the Structure column of Table 12.2. N2O: N≡N–O with a lone pair on the end N and three lone pairs on O. NO: N=O with a lone pair and one unpaired electron on N and two lone pairs on O. N2O2: O=N–N=O with a lone pair on each N and two on each O. NO2: O–N=O with one unpaired electron on N. N2O4: two NO2 units joined by an N–N bond, each N with one N–O and one N=O bond.
